questions.stem: The ancient Greek concept of "mimesis, a term used in the works of Plato, Aristotle, and other Greek philosophers in discussions of representational art-visual, performance, or literary art that aims to depict the real world-is a foundational concept of the Western philosophy of aesthetics. Mimesis is typically translated as "imitation" in modern editions of ancient Greek texts, but scholar Stephen Halliwell warns that this is overly reductive: "imitation" implies that art merely copies-and is thus by definition entirely derivative of-a reality that exists outside and prior to the work of art, and translating "mimesis" thusly obscures the multifaceted ways in which the ancient Greeks understood the relationship between art and reality. Which statement, if true, would most directly support the claim by Halliwell presented in the text?

options.A: One of the earliest appearances of mimesis's root word, mimos, can be found in an ancient Greek tragedy in reference to dramatic impersonation, and the mim- root came to be generally associated with the musical and poetic arts by the fifth century BCE.
options.B: Both Plato's and Aristotle's theorizations of mimesis examine the psychological effects that works of art induce in the viewer or listener.
options.C: Although several of Plato's earliest philosophical works discuss aesthetic ideas, the term "mimesis" doesn't appear in Plato's discussions of art until Cratylus, a relatively late work.
options.D: Although Plato's writings typically characterize representational art as an inferior reflection of the physical world, Aristotle suggests that mimesis can refer to art's capacity to envision hypothetical conditions that could, but don't yet, exist.

questions.stem: Among the most visited art museums in the world, the Galleria dell'Accademia in Florence had approximately 1.7 million visitors in 2019. The Galleria dell'Accademia also offers virtual tours that art lovers can view online for free. Although there were initial concerns that people who viewed the virtual tours would then consider an in-person visit unnecessary, museum administrators claim that their surveys of in-person visitors show that those concerns were unjustified. Which statement, if true, would most directly support the administrators' claim?

options.A: Many surveyed visitors to the Galleria dell'Accademia indicated that the virtual tours convinced them to plan an in-person visit.
options.B: Most surveyed visitors to the Galleria dell'Accademia indicated that they were unaware of the virtual tours before their first in-person visit.
options.C: Most surveyed visitors to the Galleria dell'Accademia indicated that they lived somewhere other than Florence.
options.D: Many surveyed visitors to the Galleria del'Accademia indicated that they would likely view the virtual tours in order to reminisce about their in-person visit.

questions.stem: Sandra Cisneros's 1984 novella The House on Mango Street made a lasting impact on US literature. Its depiction of Mexican American culture inspired later authors to examine their own heritage within their fictional works. Also influential was the book's portrayal of the main character, Esperanza, during a pivotal year of her youth. This insightful depiction of a preteen girl encouraged authors who, like Cisneros herself, are Latina to use fictional works to examine experiences from their own youth. Which statement, if true, would most strongly support the claim in the underlined sentence?

options.A: In interviews, a number of Latina authors say that The House on Mango Street inspired them to write about their own adolescence in their novels.
options.B: In published writings, several prominent authors who are not Latina say that reading The House on Mango Street influenced their approach to writing fiction.
options.C: The House on Mango Street has sold over six million copies and is one of the most commonly read books among high school and university students in the US.
options.D: Since 1984, new novels about young Latina characters by Latina authors have often been compared to The House on Mango Street.

questions.stem:
Botanist Rui Alvarez compared seed germination under three conditions: bare soil, a thin layer of fallen leaves, and a thick layer of fallen leaves. Germination was highest under the thin layer and lowest under the thick layer. These results support Alvarez's claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: seeds germinate only when no leaves cover the soil.
options.B: any amount of leaf litter prevents seeds from receiving water.
options.C: thick leaf litter always increases the amount of light reaching seeds.
options.D: a modest amount of leaf litter can aid germination, but too much can hinder it.

questions.explanation: D is correct because it accounts for both findings: the thin layer outperformed bare soil, whereas the thick layer performed worst.

questions.stem:
Historian Mina Okafor compared nineteenth-century ship captains' logs with repair records from the ports those ships visited. The logs mentioned fewer repairs than the port records did, and the difference was largest after periods of rough weather. Okafor argues that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: port records can reveal maintenance that captains' logs omit.
options.B: captains accurately recorded every repair made during rough weather.
options.C: ships required fewer repairs after periods of rough weather.
options.D: repair records are useful only when captains' logs are unavailable.

questions.explanation: A is correct because the port records consistently contain repair evidence absent from the logs, especially after rough weather.

questions.stem:
In a novel, the narrator insists that she has never entered the abandoned station. A few pages later, however, she describes a painted ceiling that cannot be seen from any window or doorway. This detail supports the interpretation that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: the station's ceiling was painted after the narrator left town.
options.B: every resident of the town has entered the station.
options.C: the narrator may be withholding information about her experience at the station.
options.D: the narrator learned about the ceiling from a published photograph.

questions.explanation: C is correct because the narrator's knowledge of a hidden feature conflicts with her claim that she has never entered the building.

questions.stem:
Two groups of music students practiced the same four short passages. One group practiced each passage repeatedly before moving to the next; the other alternated among the passages. On a later test using a new passage, the alternating group adjusted to changes in rhythm more successfully. The result supports the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: repeated practice prevents students from remembering a familiar passage.
options.B: alternating among tasks can improve the transfer of a skill to unfamiliar material.
options.C: students learn rhythm only when they practice a single passage.
options.D: the new passage was identical to the four practice passages.

questions.explanation: B is correct because the alternating group's stronger performance on unfamiliar material is evidence of skill transfer.

questions.stem:
Researchers observed that birds at noisy urban sites began singing earlier in the morning than birds at quiet sites. When temporary sound barriers reduced the noise, the urban birds gradually returned to later singing times. The findings suggest that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: urban birds are genetically unable to sing after sunrise.
options.B: sound barriers permanently prevent birds from singing.
options.C: quiet-site birds cannot change when they begin singing.
options.D: the timing of the urban birds' songs is a flexible response to environmental noise.

questions.explanation: D is correct because the birds changed their timing when noise conditions changed, indicating a flexible environmental response.

questions.stem:
Engineers poured equal amounts of hot water into three cups with different shapes. The wide, shallow cup cooled fastest, and the tall, narrow cup cooled slowest. The results support the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: a liquid's exposed surface area can affect how quickly it cools.
options.B: cup shape has no relationship to cooling rate.
options.C: hot water always cools fastest in the tallest container.
options.D: the amount of water determines the color of a cup.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The wider exposed surface coincided with faster cooling while water amount was held constant.

questions.stem:
After rain erased part of an ant trail, ants initially wandered near the gap. Once a few ants crossed it, later ants followed nearly the same new path. The observations support the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: ants permanently abandon every trail touched by rain.
options.B: a small number of ants can help reestablish a route that others then follow.
options.C: later ants avoid paths used by earlier ants.
options.D: rain improves ants' ability to see distant landmarks.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The later ants' convergence on the path established by early crossers supports route reestablishment.

questions.stem:
Students studied the same diagrams either by copying labels only or by explaining each relationship in their own words. On a transfer task, the explanation group more accurately applied the diagrams to a new system. The findings support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: copying labels prevents students from remembering any diagram.
options.B: transfer tasks measure handwriting speed only.
options.C: generating explanations can help learners apply relationships in a new context.
options.D: students can learn a diagram only by memorizing its labels.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The explanation group's advantage on a new system provides evidence of stronger transfer.

questions.stem:
Dyed fabric samples were displayed under bright light, dim light, or no light for six months. Bright-light samples faded most, dim-light samples faded less, and stored samples changed little. The evidence supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: fabric color becomes darker whenever light levels rise.
options.B: stored fabric fades faster than displayed fabric.
options.C: light level has no effect on dyed material.
options.D: greater light exposure can accelerate fading in dyed fabric.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The ordered fading pattern across light levels directly supports an exposure effect.

questions.stem:
A company allowed one department to choose two remote-work days each week. Employee output remained stable, while unscheduled absences declined relative to the previous six months. These results support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: the flexible schedule reduced absences without lowering measured output in that department.
options.B: remote work doubled every employee's output.
options.C: the department stopped tracking absences.
options.D: flexible schedules always improve output in every workplace.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The conclusion is limited to the two measured outcomes and does not overgeneralize beyond the pilot.

questions.stem:
In stream sections where native mussels were reintroduced, suspended particles declined and water clarity increased. Nearby sections without mussels showed little change. The comparison supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: mussels increased the number of suspended particles.
options.B: filtering by the mussels likely contributed to clearer water in the reintroduction sections.
options.C: water clarity changed equally in all stream sections.
options.D: clear water prevents mussels from filtering.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The between-section difference is consistent with mussel filtration contributing to clarity.

questions.stem:
Packaging made from compressed mushroom fibers protected glass jars during short drops as well as foam packaging did. During long storage in humid conditions, however, the mushroom packaging softened. The results support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: mushroom packaging performs better in every condition.
options.B: foam packaging softens immediately after a short drop.
options.C: mushroom-fiber packaging can handle brief impacts but may need moisture protection for humid storage.
options.D: humidity strengthens compressed mushroom fibers.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The choice accounts for both comparable impact performance and the observed humidity weakness.

questions.stem:
Singers practiced a difficult interval either at full speed only or first at reduced speed and then progressively faster. Both groups improved, but the progressive group sang the interval more accurately in the final test. The result supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: full-speed practice prevents all musical improvement.
options.B: reduced-speed practice eliminates the need for a final test.
options.C: accuracy is unrelated to how a passage is practiced.
options.D: gradually increasing speed can improve accuracy on a difficult vocal passage.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The progressive group's higher final accuracy supports the gradual-speed approach.

questions.stem:
At stops where shelters were installed, more riders waited for the bus during light rain than had waited there before installation. Ridership at unsheltered stops changed little. The evidence supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: shelters can make bus use more attractive during rainy conditions.
options.B: bus shelters cause rain to fall more frequently.
options.C: unsheltered stops gained more riders than sheltered stops.
options.D: riders use buses only when shelters are unavailable.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The rain-specific increase at newly sheltered stops supports the stated practical benefit.

questions.stem:
A night-blooming plant produced a stronger scent after sunset than during the day. In field observations, moth visits also peaked after sunset, while daytime insect visits were rare. The evidence supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: the plant depends mainly on daytime insects.
options.B: the plant's scent timing is consistent with attracting nocturnal pollinators.
options.C: moths visit only flowers with no scent.
options.D: sunset causes the plant to stop producing scent.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The alignment between stronger nighttime scent and moth visits supports the claim.

questions.stem:
Residue on stone blades from one archaeological site contained starches from both grasses and underground tubers. Wear patterns also indicated repeated cutting and scraping. Together, the findings support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: the blades were used exclusively for hunting animals.
options.B: all plant residue reached the blades after burial.
options.C: the blades were used to process more than one kind of plant material.
options.D: tubers cannot be processed by scraping.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Two distinct plant residues plus use wear support multiple plant-processing functions.

questions.stem:
New users completed a software task with either text-only buttons or buttons combining text and familiar icons. The icon group finished faster, while error rates were similar. The findings support the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: icons always eliminate user errors.
options.B: text-only buttons were faster for new users.
options.C: button design has no relationship to task completion time.
options.D: icons can speed initial navigation without necessarily changing accuracy.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The conclusion matches faster completion and unchanged errors without overstating the result.

questions.stem:
Young mangroves grown in tanks with moving water developed denser root networks than those in still water. When water movement stopped, new root growth slowed. These findings support the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: water movement can influence mangrove root development.
options.B: mangrove roots grow only in completely still water.
options.C: denser roots cause all water movement to stop.
options.D: root development is fixed before a mangrove begins growing.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Both the between-tank difference and the slowdown after movement stopped support the claim.

questions.stem:
A museum added bilingual labels to half of an exhibit. Visitors who spoke the newly added language spent more time at those displays and answered more content questions correctly than at displays with one language. The results support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: bilingual labels reduce the amount of information visitors remember.
options.B: labels in visitors' preferred language can improve engagement and understanding.
options.C: all visitors prefer exhibits with no written labels.
options.D: label language affects only the physical size of a display.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The increased time and accuracy support both engagement and understanding.

questions.stem:
A farm placed porous fences across two snow-prone fields. Snow accumulated in controlled drifts behind the fences instead of covering the access road, whereas the unfenced field's road was blocked repeatedly. The comparison supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: snow fences prevent any snow from falling.
options.B: unfenced fields form fewer drifts than fenced fields.
options.C: porous fences can redirect drifting snow away from selected areas.
options.D: access roads cause snow to melt instantly.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The controlled drift location and clearer road provide direct support.

questions.stem:
Two batches of vegetables were fermented at different temperatures. The cooler batch took longer to acidify but retained a firmer texture; the warmer batch acidified faster but softened more. The findings support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: temperature affects fermentation speed but never texture.
options.B: cooler fermentation always produces softer vegetables.
options.C: both batches acidified at exactly the same rate.
options.D: fermentation temperature can involve a tradeoff between speed and texture.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The opposite patterns in acidification time and firmness establish the tradeoff.

questions.stem:
One class completed brief memory quizzes throughout a unit, while another reread the same material for an equal amount of time. On a test one week later, the quiz group recalled more key ideas. The result supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: retrieving information during study can strengthen later recall.
options.B: rereading prevents students from understanding any material.
options.C: memory quizzes measure only writing speed.
options.D: both study methods produced identical delayed recall.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The quiz group's stronger delayed performance supports retrieval practice.

questions.stem:
Two roof coatings looked equally white indoors. Under sunlight, the coating with higher measured reflectance kept the roof surface several degrees cooler. The result supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: all white coatings have identical reflectance.
options.B: solar reflectance, not visible indoor color alone, can affect roof temperature.
options.C: cooler roofs always appear darker indoors.
options.D: roof temperature determines whether sunlight reaches a building.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The coatings looked similar but differed in reflectance and temperature, isolating the relevant property.

questions.stem:
A cook reproduced a historical bread recipe using the original grain but modern yeast. The loaf's flavor resembled descriptions in period diaries, while its rising time was much shorter. The evidence supports the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: modern yeast makes every bread taste completely different.
options.B: period diaries contain precise measurements of rising time.
options.C: ingredient substitutions can preserve some qualities of a recipe while changing others.
options.D: grain type has no relationship to bread flavor.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The preserved flavor and changed rising time demonstrate selective continuity.

questions.stem:
A conservation group installed nesting tubes of three diameters for solitary bees. Medium tubes were occupied most often, while very small and very large tubes were rarely used. The result supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: bees prefer the largest possible nesting space.
options.B: tube diameter has no relationship to occupancy.
options.C: small tubes were used more often than medium tubes.
options.D: nest-tube diameter affects whether the bees use the tubes.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The strong occupancy difference across diameters directly supports the claim.

questions.stem:
Concrete blocks containing 20 percent recycled aggregate met the project's strength requirement. Blocks containing 60 percent recycled aggregate did not, although they were lighter. The findings support the conclusion that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: recycled aggregate can be used at some levels, but higher proportions may reduce strength.
options.B: any recycled aggregate makes concrete unusable.
options.C: lighter blocks are always stronger than heavier blocks.
options.D: aggregate proportion affects weight but never strength.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The two mixture results support a qualified rather than absolute conclusion.

questions.stem:
A park added benches along one shaded path but made no changes to a similar unshaded path. Older visitors began using the shaded path more frequently and paused there longer. The evidence supports the claim that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: benches cause every visitor to avoid shaded areas.
options.B: shaded seating can encourage some visitors to spend more time on a path.
options.C: the unshaded path received the same new seating.
options.D: older visitors stopped using the park after benches were added.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The usage change following the seating addition supports the limited claim.
